name: qip-numerics
purpose: In-tree, deterministic linear algebra, statistics and optimisation primitives (no threading, no FMA contraction) so two runs on the same data produce identical bits -- what makes backtests and risk numbers reproducible; DEFAULT_TOL/DEFAULT_MAX_ITERS are the shared convergence constants every iterative solver in the crate honours.

io_and_state: None; deterministic pure math, no threading, no wall clock. Dev-dependency serde_json is test-only (Cargo.toml comment at qip-numerics/Cargo.toml:11-13).
status_reason: 13 modules, 139 tests (16 embedded in sketch.rs/streaming.rs + 123 in tests/); zero I/O, zero non-test unwrap/expect/panic except two literal panic! inside #[test] fns (sketch.rs, streaming.rs -- verified in-test).

name: qip-numerics::optimisation

production_evidence: backend/crates/services/qip-optimization-engine/src/{router.rs,problem.rs} construct and route Qubo/anneal::solve_exact; qip-optimization-engine is a dependency of backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/Cargo.toml, composed into every app.
io_and_state: None; deterministic solvers, no RNG seeded from wall-clock (anneal's Rng is caller-supplied).
status_reason: 916 combined lines, 32 tests in tests/optimisation.rs; anneal::solve_exact is exactly the classical baseline ADR 0006 mandates be computed every time a quantum QAOA path runs.

name: qip-numerics::streaming
purpose: Bounded-memory streaming primitives: streaming.rs's TDigest (quantile sketch), HyperLogLog (cardinality) and Reservoir<T> (bounded reservoir sampling, capped at RESERVOIR_MAX_ROWS); online.rs's EwCovariance/RecursiveLeastSquares/StreamingPca for exponentially-weighted online estimation; sketch.rs's CountMinSketch for approximate frequency counting -- the concrete mechanism behind the platform's 'bounded retention, bounded working sets, always' rule.
io_and_state: None; all bounds are explicit constructor arguments (capacity/precision/compression), refused rather than clamped when out of range -- e.g. Reservoir::new refuses capacity 0 or > RESERVOIR_MAX_ROWS (proven by a_reservoir_refuses_an_unbounded_capacity_and_holds_its_row_count_against_a_long_stream).
status_reason: 3401 combined lines (largest module cluster in the crate), 35 tests (16 embedded: 5 in sketch.rs, 11 in streaming.rs; 19 in tests/online.rs); directly implements the platform's 'Bounded retention' standing product decision.

name: qip-compliance
purpose: The cross-cutting governance/safety plane: six controls (point-in-time truth, licensing, model risk, capital approval, signed provenance, kill switch) each built as an enforcement mechanism whose test demonstrates the unsafe action is impossible or refused, not that the safe path merely works. CompliancePlane composes all six into a ComplianceReport that states whether each is enforced and by what, including honest caveats rather than a blanket 'compliant' claim.
key_contracts: IncidentLog, Incident, Halt, HaltScope, Clearance, ResponsePolicy (incident.rs:251,66,227,32,239,160)
production_evidence: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/plane.rs:709 field `compliance: CompliancePlane`, constructed at central/plane.rs:934 `CompliancePlane::new(...)`, read via CentralPlane::compliance_report at central/plane.rs:1550; backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:5457-5458 Platform::compliance_report delegates to it, and platform.rs:13435 gates order sign-off on report.require_fully_enforced() every DECIDE-stage cycle; qip-compliance is a direct dependency of backend/crates/apps/qip-api/Cargo.toml.
io_and_state: None; every check takes an explicit timestamp (no ambient clock, per the module doc's stated house rule); limits and contributions are qip_core::Decimal.
status_reason: 8 modules, 74 tests, all in tests/ (none embedded); five of six controls are structurally enforced (no public constructor bypasses them), but signing.rs is explicitly documented as symmetric HMAC rather than asymmetric signing -- the module doc itself lists four missing production requirements (asymmetric signing, identity binding, key rotation/revocation, countersigned timestamping) and states 'None of those are in this build.'
gaps_observed: signing.rs:1-30 module doc: HMAC-SHA256 is symmetric -- whoever can verify can also sign, so a signature proves only that someone holding the key produced the artifact, never which person or service did. No KMS, no asymmetric key material in this build; ADR 0043 (proposed, per .claude/rules/architecture/00-boundaries.md) names this as one of three gaps no in-tree code may close.
plane.rs:53 ControlStatus.caveats is the mechanism that records this gap on every generated ComplianceReport rather than hiding it -- so the gap is surfaced, not silent.
